text: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety (Leander ISD). Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety | Leander ISD News Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety Aug 5, 2026 | [News & Announcements](https://news.leanderisd.org/category/homepage/news-announcements/) [Video Message](https://youtu.be/Cm6yMlYTzhs) When questions are raised about student safety, our community deserves clear, factual answers. Transparency and accountability are essential to building trust, and we welcome the opportunity to provide information about the [Leander ISD Police Department](https://www.leanderisd.org/policedepartment/) and the work underway to strengthen it. The Leander ISD Police Department is in its first year operating as an independent law enforcement agency. As with any new organization, there have been opportunities to learn, improve and grow. Throughout that process, our focus has remained unchanged: protecting our students, supporting our staff and building a police department that serves our schools with professionalism and excellence. Below are the key messages and responses to the questions we’ve received. The Texas Commission on Law Enforcement (TCOLE) confirmed it is currently investigating Leander
label: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety

text: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety (Leander ISD). ISD PD regarding “background investigations”, whether the agency vetted an employee or employees properly. During the spring 2026 semester, Leander ISD Police Chief Rogers informed incoming Superintendent Chris Clark, Ed.D., of a prior Texas Commission on Law Enforcement (TCOLE) inquiry regarding the department’s background investigation processes for new officers. At the time of this discussion, the employee whose practices were under review was no longer employed by the district. Last month, Dr. Clark contacted TCOLE for additional details and was informed that an investigation opened in October 2025 remains active. While the district is awaiting written details, TCOLE officials indicated the investigation focuses on department vetting procedures. Leander ISD remains committed to transparency and will cooperate fully with TCOLE as this matter is finalized. What is the district doing to ensure it is properly vetting employees? Leander ISD is committed to thorough and consistent hiring practices for all its employees.
label: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety

text: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety (Leander ISD). The District has reinforced its hiring and background investigation processes for the Leander ISD Police Department. All hiring managers and background investigators are completing TCOLE background investigation training this fall to ensure continued compliance with state standards. Any response to that investigation? The District has fully cooperated with TCOLE throughout this process. We are confident our hiring and background investigation practices are being followed. Additional clarifying information was provided to TCOLE in December 2025. At this time, Leander ISD has not received any further response from TCOLE. TCOLE officer license data shows eight sworn personnel have moved on from the department since its creation. Of those, four officers have a decade or more of law enforcement experience. Those same records show six new hires this summer, including an assistant police chief with nearly two decades of law enforcement experience. Three of the officers hired this summer have less than five
label: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety

text: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety (Leander ISD). years of experience. Does the district dispute any of this data? We do not dispute that LISD PD has experienced turnover, as is common with many growing law enforcement agencies. Employees leave organizations for a variety of personal and professional reasons. Our focus is on recruiting and retaining highly qualified officers who are committed to serving our students, staff and school communities. As a continuous improvement district, we continue to evaluate employee feedback and strengthen our practices to support a positive workplace and a high-performing police department. We have spoken to former officers about retention issues at the department. Does the district feel it has had retention issues this past year? What LISD PD is experiencing is no different than many new law enforcement agencies in their first year. While there have been some staffing and retention challenges, our focus remains on developing and retaining highly qualified officers who are
label: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety

text: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety (Leander ISD). committed to serving and protecting our students, staff and school communities. What is the district doing to retain qualified officers moving forward? Our focus is on recruiting and retaining highly qualified officers by offering competitive compensation, providing clear expectations through strong leadership and cultivating a culture centered on protecting and serving our students, staff and school communities. We are committed to creating an environment where officers can build long-term careers in service to the Leander ISD community. Is the district in compliance with HB 3’s requirement to have an officer at every campus? If so, how is that being achieved? Yes, Leander ISD is in compliance with the requirements of HB3. During the launch of LISD PD, the District utilized the allowable good cause exception while continuing its strong partnerships with Cedar Park and Leander police departments, as well as Travis County Sheriff’s Office to support campus safety. We anticipate
label: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety

text: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety (Leander ISD). having a dedicated School Resource Officer assigned to every middle and high school early in the 2026-27 school year and will continue phasing in school marshals at elementary campuses through the district’s implementation plan. If not, has the district filed a good cause exception, and will you please send it to us or explain to us the terms of that exemption? Yes, the LISD board has approved a [good cause exception](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1syajMJ_s7c59XurW8gk0K_MxNS768Tw_/view?usp=sharing) , which is valid for five years. We are bringing an amendment to the Board on Aug. 6 to clarify the use of school marshals on our campuses. What challenges, if any, has the district faced implementing HB 3? Like many school districts across the state of Texas, Leander ISD has faced challenges implementing HB3, particularly because many of its requirements were not accompanied by ongoing state funding, not to mention a statewide shortage of qualified law enforcement officers.
label: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety

text: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety (Leander ISD). Despite those challenges, student safety remains our highest priority. We will continue to implement the law’s requirements while recruiting and retaining officers to serve our schools. How many officer positions are currently vacant? LISD PD still needs to hire 4 officers. Do you dispute the TCOLE license data, which shows the district has 10 officers that are not in management positions? With 49 campuses, are you all 39 officers short? The premise of that calculation is not accurate. Leander ISD Board of Trustees approved a staffing model that assigns a commissioned police officer to each secondary campus and a school marshal to each elementary campus. Currently, 10 commissioned officers are assigned to secondary campuses with additional officers in the hiring and training process. A good cause exception allows the remaining secondary campuses to be temporarily supported by school marshals while those officers complete background investigations and field training. The district
label: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety

text: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety (Leander ISD). has also hired 10 school marshals to service elementary campuses with additional candidates in the hiring process. As positions are filled and TCOLE training completed, those assignments will continue to expand in accordance with the district’s implementation plan. Have all officers been issued department vehicles? Vehicle assignments are part of the department’s phased implementation plan. The Leander ISD Police Department currently has 15 vehicles in service with an additional 15 vehicles on order. Officers hired this summer are completing field training before transitioning into full operational assignments. Have all officers been issued rifles? The 2026-27 school year marks the first year the Leander ISD Police Department has operated as an independent law enforcement agency. Prior to this transition, the department operated under partnerships with local law enforcement agencies. Officers were equipped through those agencies. Throughout that time, all Leander ISD officers were armed and completed the required annual firearms qualifications.
label: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety

text: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety (Leander ISD). As part of the transition to an independent police department, all officers will be qualified and issued department rifles prior to the start of the 2026-27 school year. Does the department have a fully operational computer-aided dispatch or records management system? Yes. The Leander ISD Police Department has a fully operational computer-aided dispatch (CAD) and records management system. As part of the department’s transition to an independent law enforcement agency, these systems were implemented to support dispatching, records management and report writing. Prior to that transition, those services were provided through partnerships with local law enforcement agencies. Does the department have a permanent evidence storage process or facility? Yes. The Leander ISD Police Department has established evidence handling procedures and a permanent evidence storage was reviewed and approved by TCOLE as part of the agency’s inspection process. The district appears to have initiated a third-party review of the climate and
label: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety

text: Leander ISD’s Commitment to School Safety (Leander ISD). culture within the Police and Emergency management departments. Has the district received that final third-party review yet? Yes, a third-party review has been received. Who will have access to that report once the district receives it? The report will be shared only with select administrative personnel who have a legitimate need to know. Because it contains personnel information and sensitive safety information, access is limited to protect employee privacy and maintain the integrity of the district’s safety and security operations. text: Stadium Clear Bag Policy (Leander ISD). Stadium Clear Bag Policy | Leander ISD Stadium Clear Bag Policy Beginning in August 2019, a clear bag policy will be in place for all VARSITY football games held in Leander ISD regional stadiums- Bible, Gupton, and Monroe. Please click on the link below to see approved and non-approved bags. [Clear Bag Policy Flyer](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Y-zdDRTGzApLqRnSph43Iw5ysWMimrk4/view?usp=sharing) Clear Bag FAQs Below you will find several frequently asked questions regarding the Clear Bag Policy for varsity football games at Leander ISD Regional Stadiums. If you have additional questions, please contact the Athletic Department at 512-570-0167. Does this procedure apply to elementary and middle schools? No. However should an elementary or middle school student attend a varsity football game at an LISD Regional Stadium, the clear bag policy will be in effect for them. Will my clear bag be checked as well? Yes, all bags will be inspected at the gate. Having a clear bag
label: Stadium Clear Bag Policy

text: Stadium Clear Bag Policy (Leander ISD). will make the inspection process go faster. Where does the clear bag policy apply? The policy applies only at varsity football games in Leander ISD Regional Stadiums (Bible, Gupton, Monroe). What about the Performing Arts Centers? No. At this time the clear bag policy does not apply to events held at the Performing Arts Centers, only at varsity football games. What happens if a guest shows up at the gate with a bag that is not permitted? Guests will not be allowed to enter the venue with a non-conforming bag. Guests will be asked to return items to their vehicle. LISD will not hold or be responsible for any items left at the gate or ticket booth. Are all purses prohibited? No. Small clutch purses, with or without a handle or strap, no larger than a hand are permitted. Purses larger than this are not permitted. See [Clear Bag Flyer](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Y-zdDRTGzApLqRnSph43Iw5ysWMimrk4/view?usp=sharing)
label: Stadium Clear Bag Policy

text: Stadium Clear Bag Policy (Leander ISD). for specific measurements. What about diaper bags? Diaper bags are not allowed. Can fans bring stadium seats or chair backs? Fans are permitted to bring in their own stadium seats or chair backs provided the seat does not have any pockets or zippers. Are other school districts implementing clear bag policies? Yes. In fact, several surrounding districts will be implementing a similar policy including Round Rock, Pflugerville, Austin, Hays, and Lake Travis. Can smartphones, tablets, binoculars or cameras be carried separately from the clear bag? Yes. Phones, cameras or binoculars may be carried in by hand. Cases for these items are not allowed. If I have special medical equipment I need to have with me at all times, where do I put that? An exception will be made for medically necessary items after proper inspection. Do I have to put everything I’m carrying into a permissible bag? No. We are
label: Stadium Clear Bag Policy

text: Stadium Clear Bag Policy (Leander ISD). limiting only the type of bags carried into the venue, not items that you normally bring to a game. Therefore, you may carry items in your pockets or jacket (keys, makeup, feminine products, comb, phone, wallet, credit cards, etc.) if you choose not to put them in a clear bag or clutch. Can I bring a blanket? Yes, but it will need to be inspected at the gate. text: Attendance & Dropout Prevention (Leander ISD). Attendance & Dropout Prevention | Leander ISD Attendance & Dropout Prevention Regular and punctual attendance is the greatest single factor in school success. Texas Compulsory Attendance Law requires students to attend regularly unless otherwise exempted by law. It is the responsibility of the parent and student to cooperate and communicate with the school on all attendance matters. The key to high school graduation is strong school attendance and parental involvement. When a student is absent, parents or guardians should submit the necessary documentation as soon as possible, which is recommended within 48 hours of the absence. This documentation must justify the reason for the absence to ensure proper coding. See LISD Parent & Student Handbook for complete attendance policy. Make education a family priority. Build your child’s self-confidence

text: Attendance & Dropout Prevention (Leander ISD). as a student by recognizing when he or she does well in school. Help your child develop good study and work habits. Schedule a daily period of home study time. Help with homework when needed. Help your child develop and achieve academic goals. Meet your child ’s teachers and other school personnel. Get to know your child ’s friends and classmates. Find ways to discuss issues, subjects and course materials being covered at school. Don’t let your child risk his or her future; make sure he or she attends school every day! When Your Child is Absent All student absences must be verified in writing by a parent. We ask that you submit a signed absence note as soon as possible, even if this is beyond the recommended 48 hours of the student’s return to school after an absence. In certain situations, this documentation – for things like a medical

text: Attendance & Dropout Prevention (Leander ISD). appointment or a religious holiday – can still mean funding for the district. It is best to submit a handwritten note directly to the attendance office. However, a faxed copy of a parent’s note or a scanned and emailed copy of a parent’s note is acceptable. Both faxed and emailed notes must have an original parent’s signature (not a typed cursive font). All notes should include: Student’s full legal name Student ID# and grade Date (s) of absence Reason for absence Parent signature (not a typed font) Frequently Asked Questions What are the Texas Attendance Laws? Section 65.003 of the Texas Family Code states: (a) A child engages in truant conduct if the child is required to attend school under 25.085, Education Code, and fails to attend school on 10 or more days or parts of days within a six-month period in the same school year. What is the 90%
label: Attendance & Dropout Prevention

text: Attendance & Dropout Prevention (Leander ISD). Rule? Texas Education Code Section 25.092 states, “a student may not be given credit for a class unless the student is in attendance for at least 90 percent of the days the class is offered.” This means that students will need to make-up class time missed due to excessive absences. Even if your child has excused absences, he or she may be asked to make up class time to earn credit for classes. What if I disagree with the school? If you feel your child’s circumstances warrant additional consideration before making up class time talk with your child’s Assistant Principal about the campus attendance appeals process What is an excused absence? Excused absences are not viewed as days a student is entitled to take. Excused absences include, but are not limited to, personal illness, funeral/memorial, quarantine or weather or road conditions that make travel dangerous. What is an unexcused absence?

text: Substitutes (Leander ISD). Substitutes | Leander ISD Substitutes Substitute Teachers provide a valuable service to our students and schools. The role of Substitute Teacher is more than just filling in for absent educators – it’s an opportunity to foster a positive learning environment, ensure continuity in education, and support student achievement. As a Substitute Teacher you play an important role in the classroom and have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on the lives of students and your community . With the flexibility to choose when and where you work, this role is an excellent option for anyone seeking a part-time position that is both rewarding and impactful. HOW TO: BECOME A SUBSTITUTE WITH LEANDER ISD Application and Hiring Process We do our best to ensure substitutes are processed as quickly as possible within a timely manner and appreciate your patience during this process. Becoming a substitute teacher offers an opportunity to make a difference in education while enjoying flexibility and diverse experiences. It can be ideal for individuals who want to give back to their community, earn part-time income, gain practical classroom experience, or explore education as a potential career path. Flexibility in Schedule – Substitute teaching allows you to work on your terms, choosing
label: Substitutes

text: Substitutes (Leander ISD). when and where you work depending on your availability. This makes it suitable for individuals with other commitments or those seeking an adaptable schedule. Make an Impact – Substitutes play a crucial role in maintaining continuity for students, ensuring their learning is not disrupted when the regular teacher is unavailable. By stepping in as a substitute teacher, you help fill a critical need and ensure students continue to receive quality education, support and stability. Even in a day, you can inspire, motivate, and encourage students, making a meaningful impact in their educational journey. Community Contribution – By stepping in as a substitute, you directly support your local school district. This support reduces the strain on schools and other staff members, helping ensure every classroom has an educator present and the day continues to run smoothly. The work you do not only impacts students, but also helps their families, and the
label: Substitutes

text: Substitutes (Leander ISD). wider community, by ensuring that students are cared for and educated. Diverse Experience – Every school and every classroom is different, making every day you sub different and unique. You have the opportunity to work and interact with a range of educators, staff and students, making meaningful connections and building relationships while learning from others. It also allows you the opportunity to gain exposure to various grade levels, subjects and classroom environments. This can be beneficial when considering becoming a full time teacher to better understand your preferences and strengths white determining if a career in education is the right fit for you. Pathway to Full Time Employment – Substitute teaching is often a stepping stone for those considering full-time employment. It provides practical classroom experience that can help develop teaching skills, classroom management strategies,and allow for networking opportunities that can lead to future permanent roles. Substitute Teachers take the place of the regular teachers when they need to be absent. They have the full responsibility of the regular teacher and are expected to carry out the teacher’s lesson plans and maintain classroom management in the classroom. Instructional Assistant (IA) Substitutes take the place of instructional assistants when they are absent. They will have a professional staff member to assist them in carrying out their duties throughout the day. Instructional Assistant responsibilities vary depending on the role at that particular campus and can be SPED or Non-SPED positions. They should be able to separate the students’ behaviors from the students themselves. The training provided by Human Resources gives numerous strategies for dealing with a wide variety of “discipline problems.” The LISD Substitute Handbook stresses repeatedly that substitute teachers are never to use physical force with students. Nor should they use sarcasm with students, shout at the students, insult them, or otherwise verbally attack them. (See the Discipline section of LISD’s [Substitute Teacher Handbook)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1e5fUrHcGYwwlnfyffA2bI8zrV_6H9DPd/view) Please see additional training resources regarding classroom management located on the substitute website under training resources. What do I do at the end of the day? Check to see if the teacher you are subbing for has any after school duties you need to fulfill. You may choose to leave a note for the teacher whose place you took. The
label: Substitutes

text: Substitutes (Leander ISD). note may include feedback to the teacher on how the lesson plans were completed, as well as any information about students and student behavior that they need to know. This can be very helpful and beneficial to the teacher when they return. As for the dismissal of students, the procedures will vary at different instructional levels as well as from campus to campus. ALWAYS check with the front office if you have any questions regarding the dismissal procedures for that campus. I didn't sign up to substitute in a special education classroom. Why are there special education students in the gen ed classroom? The philosophy and strategies of inclusion and collaboration require that all students be educated in the “least restrictive environment” possible, so special needs students are always included in the “regular” classroom to the fullest possible extent. Please read more about the topic of inclusion and collaborative instruction
label: Substitutes

text: Substitutes (Leander ISD). on the [Special Education Website](https://www.leanderisd.org/specialeducation/) . I would like to work more directly with students with special needs. Does LISD provide any training? Yes, if you are interested in receiving some hands-on training in working with students with special needs contact our Substitute Coordinator, Candy Tijerina , to schedule a training time with someone from our special education staff. [[email protected]](https://www.leanderisd.org/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#92d1f3fcf6ebbcc6fbf8f7e0fbfcf3d2fef7f3fcf6f7e0fbe1f6bcfde0f5) OR 512-570-0047 Can I substitute in dual language classrooms even if I do not speak Spanish? Yes. You do not have to be bilingual to sub in our dual language classrooms. Students will be speaking Spanish to each other at times in these classrooms, however in most grade levels there are enough students who are proficient in both English and Spanish to assist in translating when needed. [View this presentation on what to expect in a dual language classroom](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1tVR1Gn7V08APveOvfItZzz9_R0CPqcxETLa%20BdXGxcU4/edit?usp=sharing) . Should substitutes allow students to visit the school nurse
label: Substitutes

text: Substitutes (Leander ISD). every time they ask to do so? Substitutes should never deny a student’s request to go to the nurse. It is the nurse’s responsibility to determine whether or not a child is ill–not the substitute teacher’s. Please make sure to check for any teachers notes regarding their bathroom policy or notes regarding certain students. Can substitute teachers share their religious beliefs or political views with students in the classroom? Like other employees of the district, substitutes must maintain a posture of “neutrality” regarding religion and political views in the classroom and in other activities and areas of the school. Substitutes should follow the teachers’ lesson plans and not introduce topics for discussion that may be disruptive or controversial. Where can I find additional substitute training resources? text: Class Ranking (Leander ISD). counselors, campus and district administrators, and board members met over the course of several months to review the current GPA and rank policy and make suggestions for changes. The three main themes which emerged from the committee meetings were: Student Choice Focus on the Whole Child Well Rounded Graduates The intent of the new policy is to allow students to select courses and pathways of study based on their individual interests instead of selecting courses solely for the intended GPA boost. The complete language to the change can be seen in [Policy EIC (Local)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1698HFxrZlorgRiOpuim0VzSEAlulQ954/view) , but significant changes are highlighted below. Courses Included in the Calculation of Weighted GPA A student’s weighted GPA will be used to calculate class rank. text: Class Ranking (Leander ISD). this purpose. Reporting Class Rank Class rank will only be reported for the top ten percent of each class. After each calculation period, students in the top ten percent will be told their exact class rank in accordance with administrative procedures. The lowest weighted GPA of students in the top ten percent, the first quartile, the second quartile, and the third quartile shall be communicated to all students in the class after each calculation period. The district shall include on the official transcript of each student in the top ten percent the student’s specific numerical rank out of the specific total class size. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) What is GPA? Grade Point Average (GPA) is a conversion of grades earned in high school into a single numerical average. In Leander ISD students receive an unweighted and weighted GPA. The unweighted GPA includes all courses taken in grades 9-12 on a
label: Class Ranking

text: Class Ranking (Leander ISD). 4.0 scale. The weighted GPA only includes certain courses (listed above) on a Level I, II and III scale. Level I courses are weighted on a 5.0 scale Level II courses are weighted on a 5.5 scale Level III courses are weighted on a 6.0 scale Why do some students receive a class rank? The state of Texas requires public schools to publish rank for the top 10 percent of students in each class. In Texas, students who are in the top 10 percent of their graduating class receive automatic admission to any public university or college in Texas, with the exception of The University of Texas. Although it can change for each graduating class, currently the University of Texas automatically admits students ranked in the top 6 percent of their class. What if I am outside the top 10 percent? Students who fall outside of the top 10 percent
label: Class Ranking

text: Class Ranking (Leander ISD). of their class will not receive a class rank. Students will be notified of the lowest weighted GPA of students in the top ten percent, the first quartile, the second quartile, and the third quartile. Will this affect college applications? As part of the committee work, Leander ISD staff contacted other school districts and institutions of higher education for feedback on the proposed policy changes. Other districts with similar policies reported no negative impacts to their students and their college applications. Universities will holistically review the student’s application for admission taking into consideration the courses available to the student as well as the courses the student completed. This information is available on the student transcript and the published school profile. Why are advanced courses weighted differently than AP/IB? Advanced Placement (AP) and International Baccalaureate (IB) courses require a comprehensive, nationally recognized end of course exam. Based on the results of
label: Class Ranking

text: Class Ranking (Leander ISD). the exam, students have the potential to earn college credit. While advanced level courses can be rigorous and prepare students for AP/IB level course work, they do not require a nationally recognized exam and do not have the potential to earn college credit. Why not weight dual credit courses? Excluding dual credit courses in the weighted GPA calculation was a difficult decision. Because these courses are not taught by a Leander ISD staff member and students only receive a final letter grade, the decision was made to exclude dual credit courses. The committee reviewed different weighting options and each scenario penalized students who took dual credit courses. Because one of the main goals of the committee was to promote student choice, the group believed including dual credit courses would have the potential to limit a student’s ability to create a personal academic plan of study. Advanced Academics: Middle School | Leander ISD Advanced Academics: Middle School Exam for Acceleration Exam for Acceleration allows Leander ISD students who have mastered the content and skills of a particular grade level or course without direct instruction to advance to the next level so they will be more appropriately challenged. When registered and taken at designated times in the district, these exams are available at no cost to eligible students. Leander ISD uses exams from the University of Texas. When tests are not available through UT, the district may use Texas Tech University Distance Education Center exams for grades K-12. These testing resources ensure standardization and objectivity of the exams. Campus counselors can provide guidance on testing and registration when needed.. See the Math Pathways tab below for information that allows students to access accelerated content in math without the need for Exam for Acceleration. [More information about Exam

text: Advanced Academics: Middle School (Leander ISD). for Acceleration](https://www.leanderisd.org/examforacceleration/) Advanced Students who wish to take the higher-level academic classes that best prepare them for college benefit greatly from advanced-course preparation in middle school. The Advanced courses that are available to Leander ISD middle school students include Math 6/7, Math 7/8, Algebra I, Geometry, Advanced Language Arts grades 6-8, and 8th-grade Social Studies. AVID for Possibilities ! [AVID](https://explore.avid.org/what-avid-is/) (Advancement Via Individual Determination) is a college and career readiness system designed to increase the number of students who enroll in four-year colleges. Although AVID serves all students, it focuses on the least served students in the academic middle. The formula is simple—raise expectations of students and, with the AVID support system in place, they will rise to the challenge. AVID students have the desire to attend college and the willingness to work hard. AVID middle school students enroll in coursework that challenges them so they can be prepared to
label: Advanced Academics: Middle School

text: Advanced Academics: Middle School (Leander ISD). access college and career coursework in high school. AVID Elective students learn organizational and study skills, work on critical thinking and asking probing questions, get academic help from peers and college and adult tutors, and participate in enrichment and motivational activities that make college seem attainable. As members of the AVID elective, self‐images improve, and students become academically successful leaders and role models for other students. The AVID elective is open to any student with the determination! [More information on AVID](https://www.leanderisd.org/avid/) Math Pathways Leander ISD aims to provide access to math instruction at a level and pace to meet the learning needs of our students. To achieve this goal, we have developed math challenge opportunities in elementary that lead to Math Pathways beginning in 5th grade and continuing through high school. All students will be offered challenge and support to develop strong foundations that lead to the pathways that best

Students currently enrolled in Math Pathway 2 remain enrolled as long as data indicates it is instructionally appropriate. In 2023 Senate Bill 2124 passed, which requires Texas Public School Districts to use STAAR and/or a local measures to automatically enroll students in the top two quintiles (top 40%) of STAAR and/or a local measure. Leander ISD uses a combination of STAAR and MAP as our local measure to automatically place students in Math Pathway 2. To ensure all students reach their full potential in math, teachers regularly assess understanding through classwork and multiple assessments. Teachers, students and families work in unison to develop personalized learning plans in the event additional support in mastering concepts is needed. The personalized learning plan will leverage student strengths while targeting specific areas for growth. In the event the plan does not lead to significant progress, placement in Math Pathway 1 (grade-level math) may be recommended to ensure a solid mathematical foundation. Ask yourself these questions to see if you’re eligible for ACC Free Tuition and find out what’s included for you.

When did you earn your high school diploma or TX GED®?
If you have graduated from a high school in the ACC service area as part of the class of 2024 through the class of 2028, or completed your homeschool program/TX GED® equivalency in the same time frame, you may be eligible!

Where do you live ?
If you live in the service area covered by ACC, you may be eligible. This encompasses 7,000 square miles immediately around the City of Austin. High school graduates must have received their diploma from a high school in ACC’s service area.

Will you have to pay other fees?

text:
Vista Ridge College & Career Center - FINANCIAL AID & SCHOLARSHIPS (text in an image on the page): THE FINANCIAL AID PROCESS
Finding financial aid can seem overwhelming when you’re trying to get ready for college or career school. The U.S. Department of Education’s office of Federal Student Aid is here to help you get the money you need to pay for your education.

PREPARATION
Scholarships and state aid can help cover the cost of college or career school, but you may find yourself in need of federal assistance.

Begin saving early.

Many states have college funding programs. Ask a guidance counselor or your college financial aid office for more information.

Look for scholarships through your state or college as well as national and community organizations.

It’s time to apply for financial aid.

FAFSA®
label: Vista Ridge College & Career Center - FINANCIAL AID & SCHOLARSHIPS

text:
Vista Ridge College & Career Center - FINANCIAL AID & SCHOLARSHIPS (text in an image on the page): The FAFSA is the Free Application for Federal Student Aid and is the only way to apply for federal student aid. The schools you list on your application will use FAFSA information to evaluate your financial need and determine how much federal aid you are eligible to receive. Many states and colleges also use information from your FAFSA to provide their own financial aid.

Each October, the FAFSA is available for the next school year. It is best to fill it out as early as you can because some aid is first come, first served.

When you complete the FAFSA, you’ll need to provide personal and tax information. You may be able to automatically retrieve your tax information from the IRS.

Complete the FAFSA online at fafsa.gov. Make sure to fill out and submit the FAFSA each year you are in college.
label: Vista Ridge College & Career Center - FINANCIAL AID & SCHOLARSHIPS

text:
Vista Ridge College & Career Center - FINANCIAL AID & SCHOLARSHIPS (text in an image on the page): After you submit your FAFSA, you’ll receive your Student Aid Report (SAR). Your SAR summarizes the information in your FAFSA. Review it and make corrections if needed.

Your FAFSA helps your school determine the types of federal student aid you are eligible to receive.

TYPES OF FEDERAL STUDENT AID
As the largest provider of financial aid, the U.S. Department of Education’s office of Federal Student Aid provides grants, loans, and work-study funds.

GRANTS | LOANS | WORK-STUDY
Grants are free money that do not have to be repaid. | Student loans are real loans (like a car or home loan) that need to be repaid with interest. | A work-study job gives you the opportunity to earn money to help pay your educational expenses.

AWARD
label: Vista Ridge College & Career Center - FINANCIAL AID & SCHOLARSHIPS

text:
Vista Ridge College & Career Center - FINANCIAL AID & SCHOLARSHIPS (text in an image on the page): Your award letter explains the combination of federal grants, loans, and work-study a college is offering you. The offer might also contain state and institutional aid. If you receive award letters from multiple colleges or career schools, you should compare them and decide which school works best for you.

COLLEGE
Every year, millions of new students attend college or career school for the first time. Your college or career school has a financial aid office to help guide you along the way.

BEYOND EDUCATION

WORKFORCE
When you take the time to plan for your education and let Federal Student Aid help you along the way, you’ll be setting the foundation for a bright future and success in the workforce.

REPAYMENT
Once you leave school, you will need to repay your student loans. Contact your loan servicer to discuss your repayment options.

Federal Student Aid

text:
Vista Ridge College & Career Center - TYPES OF AID (text in an image on the page): TYPES OF AID

Need help paying for college or career school? Federal Student Aid, an office of the U.S. Department of Education, may be able to help you get the financial aid you need for college. We provide more than $150 billion in financial aid every year.

Federal Student Aid offers three types of financial aid.

1 | Financial aid that generally doesn’t have to be repaid.
Federal Pell Grant:
• For undergraduates with financial need.

Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grant (FSEOG):
• For undergraduates with exceptional financial need at participating schools.

Teacher Education Assistance for College and Higher Education (TEACH) Grant:
• For undergraduates and graduate students who are going to school to become elementary or secondary school teacher.
• A student must agree to teach in a high-need field at a low-income school for at least four years within eight years after graduation.
label: Vista Ridge College & Career Center - TYPES OF AID

text:
Vista Ridge College & Career Center - TYPES OF AID (text in an image on the page): • Failure to live up to this agreement means that the grant is converted to a loan and must be repaid.

Iraq and Afghanistan Service Grant:
• For students with a parent or guardian who died after the events of 9/11 as a result of military service in Iraq or Afghanistan.
• To qualify, a student must have been under the age of 24 at the time of his or her parent or guardian’s death or enrolled in college or career school at least part-time.

2 | Borrowed money for college or career school; your loans must be repaid with interest.
Direct PLUS Loan:
• For graduate and professional students and for parents of dependent undergraduates.
• Borrower is responsible for all interest.

Direct Subsidized Loan:
• For undergraduates.
• Interest is paid by the U.S. Department of Education while the student is in school and during periods of deferment.
label: Vista Ridge College & Career Center - TYPES OF AID

text:
Vista Ridge College & Career Center - TYPES OF AID (text in an image on the page): Direct Unsubsidized Loan:
• For undergraduates and graduate students.
• Borrower is responsible for all interest.

Federal Perkins Loan:
• For undergraduate and graduate students.
• Loan made by participating school.
• No interest accrues while the student is in school or in a grace period and during periods of deferment.

WHY GET FEDERAL STUDENT LOANS?
Loans are an investment in your future and can be a great way to pay for school. Compared to private student loans, federal student loans often have
• lower fixed interest rates,
• flexible repayment options, and
• many benefits that you won’t find elsewhere.

3 | A federal work program through which undergraduates and graduate students at participating schools earn money to help pay for school.

OTHER SOURCES OF FINANCIAL AID
You also may be eligible for financial aid from
• other government agencies,
• the state where you live,
label: Vista Ridge College & Career Center - TYPES OF AID

text:
Vista Ridge College & Career Center - TYPES OF AID (text in an image on the page): • the college you attend, or
• a nonprofit or private organization.

Learn more about these options at StudentAid.gov/types.

To apply for financial aid from the federal government, complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA®) at www.fafsa.ed.gov. Your school will use information from your FAFSA® to compile your financial aid offer, which may include a combination of grants, loans, and work-study. Many states and schools also use information from the FAFSA® to award other types of aid.

Remember, federal student aid must be used for school expenses such as tuition, room and board, and books and supplies.

If you have questions or need any assistance, contact the financial aid office at your college or career school or visit StudentAid.gov.

text:
mLISD Empowered Learning - Technology Application TEKS (text in an image on the page): Texas TEKS Curriculum

Kindergarten - Texas Tech Apps
Learn to type all letter keys and:
- Learn the parts of a computer
- Understand how to use a mouse & trackpad
- Develop typing accuracy with grade-level ELA content
- Understand responsible technology use

1st Grade - Texas Tech Apps
Learn to type all letter and number keys and:
- Learn about software and hardware
- Practice capitalization & punctuation
- Understand positive online communication
- Explore & apply the design process

2nd Grade - Texas Tech Apps
Learn to type all letter and number keys and:
- Build speed & accuracy with contextual practice
- Understand the basics of cybersecurity & online searching
- Address problem keys in adaptive lessons
- Learn about basic computer applications

3rd Grade - Texas Tech Apps
Learn to type all letter and number keys and:
- Explore scenario-based digital citizenship lessons
label: mLISD Empowered Learning - Technology Application TEKS

text:
mLISD Empowered Learning - Technology Application TEKS (text in an image on the page): - Generate original creative writing content
- Troubleshoot software & hardware issues
- Explore variables, conditionals, & algorithms

4th Grade - Texas Tech Apps
Learn to type all letter and number keys and:
- Type grade-specific ELA passages
- Use keyword searches
- Boost speed with timed questions
- Understand digital ethics & online safety

5th Grade - Texas Tech Apps
Learn to type all keys and:
- Practice typing emails
- Create charts, graphs, & spreadsheets
- Develop test-taking skills
- Explore emerging technology & computer systems

6th Grade - Texas Tech Apps
Learn to type all keys and:
- Improve typing speed with ELA lessons
- Recognize & respond to cyberbullying
- Practice document formatting
- Generate block & text-based code
label: mLISD Empowered Learning - Technology Application TEKS

text:
Mrs. Christman's Classes - Urinary System (text in an image on the page): Four Processes in Urine Formation

Glomerular Filtration
Water, salts, nutrient molecules, and waste molecules move from the glomerulus to the inside of the Bowman’s capsule. These small molecules are called the glomerular filtrate.

Tubular Reabsorption
Nutrient and salt molecules are actively reabsorbed from the convoluted tubule into the peritubular capillary network, proximal convoluted tubule, and water flows passively.

Tubular Secretion
Certain molecules (e.g. H+ and penicillin) are actively secreted from the peritubular capillary network into the distal tubule.

Water Reabsorption
Water is reabsorbed from the collecting duct by osmosis. Water reabsorption in the collecting duct increases the concentration of the filtrate.

1. Glomerular filtration:
H₂O & solutes move from blood into nephron

2. Tubular reabsorption:
Useful substances move from filtrate into blood

3. Tubular secretion:
Wastes & excess substances move from blood into filtrate

4. Water reabsorption:
H₂O moves from filtrate into blood

text:
Mrs. Crandus - Course Resources (text in an image on the page): What do bacteria look like?
Bacteria are single-celled organisms, although they may occur in groups of cells. Two common shapes for bacteria are short or long rods, or spheres. The main characteristic that distinguishes bacteria from organisms in the Eukarya group is that they do not have membrane-enclosed compartments such as a nucleus, mitochondria, and vacuoles.
label: Mrs. Crandus - Course Resources

text: Mrs. Crandus - Course Resources (text in an image on the page): Bacterial shapes. Some bacteria are shaped like long or short rods. Spheres are another common shape for bacteria. a. This Escherichia coli bacterium is a short rod that lives in the human intestinal tract. Most strains are harmless to us, but some cause food poisoning. E. coli have whip-like tails that help them swim. b. Salmonella bacteria are also short rods. These bacteria are present in the intestinal tracts of humans and other animals, although they are usually killed or pass through the body before they grow enough to cause problems. Lone Star Company - Teams (text in an image on the page): ARMED DRILL

WHAT DO WE DO?
Completing a series of pre-planned movements while displaying strong control of an 8.5 lb model rifle, this includes everything from basic marching skills in a regulation (by the book) competition to spinning the rifles in exhibition (fancy performance) competition. This team has a history of helping cadets develop good bearing and knowledge within the program and often helps drive cadets on their road to leadership positions.
label: Lone Star Company - Teams

text:
Lone Star Company - Teams (text in an image on the page): UNARMED DRILL

WHAT DO WE DO?

Unarmed is a drill team that performs in two different ways at competitions. Regulation drill is precise military marching with a set of orders and movements that are standard across units. We also practice Exhibition drill which is marching as well, but combined with rhythmic body movements and more flourish. Unarmed focuses on both of these types of performances, and helps to teach cadets basic drill knowledge that will greatly benefit them in their NJROTC classes.
label: Lone Star Company - Teams

text:
Lone Star Company - Teams (text in an image on the page): COLOR GUARD

WHAT DO WE DO?

Color Guard consists of a 4 person team, 2 flags and 2 rifles, that march in accordance with our drill manual. We are the main face of our program performing at a variety of events. We perform at football games, private events, and ceremonies. We also compete against other schools at multiple competitions.
label: Lone Star Company - Teams

text:
Lone Star Company - Teams (text in an image on the page): PHYSICAL FITNESS

WHAT DO WE DO?
PT team is a team built to help instill discipline, collaboration skills, and physical fitness. We compete at drill meets against other schools as well as postal competitions. Typical exercises completed at drill meets are pushups, situps, and running. The PT team is a great place to be if you find yourself with lots of energy and motivation.
label: Lone Star Company - Teams

text:
Lone Star Company - Teams (text in an image on the page): MARKSMANSHIP

WHAT DO WE DO?

Marksmanship is a team where cadets shoot lead pellets with an air rifle at electronic targets in one of three positions: prone, standing, and kneeling. We compete at skills meets, postals, and other competitions. Marksmanship is a unique team that will instill a sense of patience, discipline, and commitment in anyone willing to stick to it and make an active effort to be on the team. There is only one requirement to join, you have to attend the safety brief and pass an assessment prior to joining the team.

Welcome to Vista Ridge High School and AVID!! Your AVID (Advancement Via Individual Determination) class will prepare you for the entrance into a four-year college. The AVID curriculum places emphasis on analytical reading and writing, study and test taking skills, organizational skills, note-taking practices, research projects, and preparation for college entrance and placement exams. The continuation of financial literacy study includes lessons on banking, saving, employment, insurance, and tax credits. Student Agency and self-confidence are developed to prepare students to become purpose-driven leaders. The 10th-grade AVID course uniquely blends academic, financial, digital literacy, and leadership skills, equipping students for future endeavors.

text:
Mrs. Duncan - Euro (text in an image on the page): AP European History Curriculum Explained

AP European History is an elective history course not required by Texas. The curriculum has been created by college professors and high school teachers, and includes what would be included in a college World History course, as well as what skills need to be mastered. College Board, the entity that runs the Advanced Placement (AP), PSAT and SAT, approves the curriculum that is sent to all authorized teachers around the world..

In order for a class to be called AP, the teacher must teach the curriculum and skills the College Board requires. All subjects are taught objectively and include all sides of the subject, as well as primary sources that explain the people, events, concepts and theories.

For more information on the AP European course, please visit AP Central. To see the detailed curriculum, please click here (curriculum starts on page 30).

Mr. Huddleston - AVID 9th Grade (text in an image on the page): Mr. Huddleston | Room 1116
justin.huddleston@leanderisd.org | Phone 512-570-1800 Ext. 41861

AVID I
2026-2027

Welcome to Vista Ridge High School and AVID!! Your AVID (Advancement Via Individual Determination) class will prepare you for the entrance into a four-year college. The AVID curriculum places emphasis on analytical reading and writing, study and test taking skills, organizational skills, note-taking practices, research projects, and preparation for college entrance exams. The class will also include Professional Communication assignments and financial literacy.

TECHNOLOGY

- Throughout this course, students will be working with online software, which involves use of the Internet
- We highly encourage our students to participate in our districts mLISD laptop initiative or regularly bring their own laptops or tablets from home.
- We will use Google Classroom to post and submit assignments and keep track of resources that students can access and use when needed throughout the year.
label: Mr. Huddleston - AVID 9th Grade

text:
Mr. Huddleston - AVID 9th Grade (text in an image on the page): - Per Texas Law, cell phones, smart watches, tablets, and headphones WILL NOT be allowed during the school day.

GRADING POLICIES

- NO LATE Note, Organization, and planner will be accepted.
- Late work must be submitted by the end of the 3 week grading period for a maximum grade of 70
- You must come prepared to class on tutorial days with a completed TRF Form
- Students are expected to complete 6 hours of community service each grading period.

GRADES

Category | Percentage
Curriculum | 30.0%
Focused Notes | 20.0%
Binder/Planner Organization | 20.0%
Tutorials | 20.0%
Community Service | 10.0%
label: Mr. Huddleston - AVID 9th Grade

text:
Mr. Huddleston - AVID 9th Grade (text in an image on the page): CLASS STRUCTURE & CURRICULUM
Students participate in activities that incorporate strategies focused on writing, inquiry, collaboration, organization, and reading (WICOR) to support their academic growth.
• Monday - Thursday students will utilize the AVID curriculum for ½ of the class.
• Monday - Thursday students will participate in tutorials for the other ½ of the class.
• Fridays are dedicated to team building, academic support, guest speakers, etc...

ASSESSMENT
AVID students will be assessed using a variety of performance-based assessments. They will be assessed on AVID skills such as a well-organized notebook, participation in tutorials, and note-taking, as well as their performance on timed writings, practice college entrance tests, participation in Socratic Seminars, participation in their community, and other activities.

TUTORIALS
label: Mr. Huddleston - AVID 9th Grade

text:
Mr. Huddleston - AVID 9th Grade (text in an image on the page): During tutorial time students work with tutors, who may be current and/or former AVID students, AP students, current college students, or college graduates to improve their understanding of academic skills.
• Students are required to turn in a Tutorial Request Form (TRF) at the beginning of class
• Students will need to bring their resources that pertain to the TRF to class.
• Students will be active participants during the tutorial process.

SUPPLIES
• Binder OR accordion folder
• Planner
• Tabs/dividers if using a binder
• Pencil pouch
  o Black or blue pens
  o Highlighters (any color)
  o Pencils/erasers, Expo Markers
• Notebook paper
• Expo Markers
• Tissues

ATTENDANCE
• It is the EXPECTATION for you to get missing work BEFORE you come back to class after an absence.
• Please check Google Classroom for any assignments you may have missed.

text: Mr. Huddleston - US History (text in an image on the page): Founding documents: Declaration of Independence and Constitution, Bill of Rights; Principles of republicanism & "exceptionalism" & Tocqueville's 5 values | Westward expansion; Native American policies; expansionist ideology and Industrial Revolution; urbanization; immigration | Progressive movement and many of its reforms | Spanish-American War in 1898 and expansion to Caribbean/Pacific; WWI breaks out in Europe; US entry 1917 | Flourishing of the 1920s: freedom in culture, art, and music, rise of consumerism, and materialism. Wealth, privilege, and mass culture. Impact of the Great Depression on the people and government response to the economic crisis. | Rise of dictators in Europe; Outbreak of WWII and US entry; transformation of US society into war mode | United States and the Soviet Union begin the Cold War: investment in nuclear and social changes. Korean War, Vietnam, consumerism: boomers experience economic boom; baby boomers; increased spending and prosperity; mass media, especially television; many still lived in poverty and suffered discrimination. A response to this is the Civil Rights Movement. US involvement in Vietnam and its effects at home and abroad. Protest at home and a backlash against the conformity of the 1950s led to a growing counterculture. | African American activists and other groups begin to win legal and social changes. The courts, Congress, and the presidency expand opportunity in education, housing, and voting rights. Other reform programs expanded in Great Society. | The rise of the conservative movement as a backlash to the perceived liberalism of the New Deal and Great Society. Under President Nixon: detente (relaxation of tensions) with the Soviet Union and China. President Reagan's conservative agenda. President Bush is swept into office in a Republican landslide. The Soviet Union collapses and the Cold War ends. | The economic growth and technological innovations experienced since 1980 have changed the workplace and the presidency. Debates over the role of government and the US in the world continue. The US faces new challenges as well. The 2000 election is disputed. The September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks lead to a new war on Terror. The election of Barack Obama is historic. The recession of 2008. Osama bin Laden is killed in 2011. The Affordable Care Act is debated and enacted in 2012.

VRHS Instructional Coaching (text in an image on the page): VRHS INSTRUCTIONAL COACH

KRISTEN KELLY

Hello! My name is Kristen Kelly and I am so happy to serve at the Instructional Coach for Vista Ridge High School! I have experience with all levels of Spanish through 5 AP and served as the Department Chair for World Languages. I am passionate about supporting teachers, and helping students achieve success. I do not know everything, but I will find answers for you and do what I can to be a resource. I believe in the power of a growth mindset and life-long learning, and my goal is to make your job easier!

WHAT AN INSTRUCTIONAL COACH IS | WHAT AN INSTRUCTIONAL COACH IS NOT
• A colleague who offers feedback to improve teaching. | • An administrator who evaluates a teacher's teaching.
• A colleague who co-plans lessons. | • A colleague who plans lessons for a teacher.
label: VRHS Instructional Coaching

text:

• A colleague who provides resources. | • A colleague who reports confidential conversations to admin.
• A colleague who listens and remains confidential. |

FUN FACTS ABOUT ME
• I graduated from The University of Texas (Hook ‘em!).
• I studied Spanish, Portuguese, and Linguistics.
• I have two cats, Mae and Mia, and a dog, Mika.

HOW I CAN SUPPORT YOU
• Coaching cycle
• Creating LEADS/SLO goals
• Data reflection
• Resource connections
• Technology Integration

A literal equation is an equation involving two or more variables. Unlike traditional equations where you often solve for one variable in terms of numbers, in a literal equation, you solve for one variable in terms of the other variables.

Tracy Palmer - Adv. Algebra II Syllabus (text in an image on the page): VR VISTA RIDGE HIGH SCHOOL
CELL PHONE Best Practices

VRHS believes consistent cell phone practices are crucial for fostering an optimal learning environment by increasing student engagement, focus, and collaboration, which in turn enhances learning outcomes. These practices also aim to decrease distractions by minimizing the negative impacts of excessive phone use during the school day.

What
All personal devices, including cell phones, wearable devices (smartwatches), and headphones/earbuds, are not permitted for use in the classroom. These devices must be out of sight and silenced in classrooms and restrooms (electronic passes can be made with a computer).

Where
Personal devices must be stored in student’s backpack or school bag; not directly on their person. If a warning is given and a student does not have a school bag, the student is required to leave their device in the AP office.
label: Tracy Palmer - Adv. Algebra II Syllabus

text:
Tracy Palmer - Adv. Algebra II Syllabus (text in an image on the page): If parents/guardians need to contact their student, please send the student an email or contact the front office at (512) 570-1800.

When
Personal devices are not to be used during instructional time (8:05am to 3:35pm), but may be used before and after school.

Students will be able to access personal devices to meet documented medical or accommodation requirements.

Consequences
Students found to be in non-compliance with these practices will receive a warning from the teacher along with attempted guardian contact. The next incident will result in a referral to their AP. Repeated violations may result in parents or guardians being required to pick up personal devices from VRHS and students may lose the privilege to bring a personal device to school. Continued violations will result in additional consequences in alignment with the Leander ISD Student Code of Conduct.
label: Tracy Palmer - Adv. Algebra II Syllabus

label: Building the Future of Leander ISD, Together

Safety Shoutout: Crosswalks Please encourage your students to use the crosswalk at Park Street where we have a crossing guard on duty, rather than the crosswalk at the entrance to Gupton Stadium. We have heard many reports from the community about near misses at the Gupton Crosswalk. The inattention goes both ways - driver's failing to yield to an active crosswalk, and students, particularly on bicycles, failing to activate the crosswalk and cross safely. Whether your student is a drive, walker, or rider, please talk to them about being hyper aware in the crosswalk, and using the Park Street crossing with a guard whenever possible.
